task.description:
TEST-DESIGNER pass (WF-02 Step 3) on REQ-168. ELIXIR-DEV already wrote an initial test suite (test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs, 16 tests, all passing per prior gates' independent reruns). This is the highest-stakes WASM module so far -- its whole reason for existing is preventing a real, live-verified BEAM-node-crashing hazard in wasmex. Your job is a MUTATION-DRIVEN review and strengthening pass: read the shipped memory_guard.ex in full, then find and fill real coverage gaps by actually mutating the implementation locally and confirming the existing suite fails to catch each mutation before adding a test that does. Use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching mix commands. Revert every mutation before finishing.

CRITICAL SAFETY INSTRUCTION, read before doing anything: NEVER call MemoryGuard.read/4, MemoryGuard.write/4, or any Wasmex.Memory function directly (live) with an offset/length magnitude at or above roughly 2^40 -- lib/letflow/design/req168-wasm-memory-isolation.md section 1.4 live-reproduced a genuine SIGABRT (full OS process abort, exit code 134) at that magnitude on this exact dependency version. Every one of your own mutation-testing probes involving a large magnitude MUST target the PURE check_bounds/3 function only, never a live Wasmex.Memory call. If you are unsure whether a probe is safe, don't run it live -- test it against check_bounds/3 directly instead.
acceptance_criteria: Mutate check_bounds/3's offset-range check (step 3) to use >= instead of > (i.e. reject offset == memory_size, which the design says should be ALLOWED for a zero-length access exactly at the end boundary) and confirm an existing test catches this; if not, add one.

Mutate check_bounds/3's end-of-range check (step 4) to compute range_end using a native-sized arithmetic simulation (e.g. explicitly truncate/mask the sum to 64 bits before comparing) and confirm an existing test would catch a false-accept this could theoretically produce -- if the existing tests only use magnitudes where truncation wouldn't matter, add a test at a magnitude specifically chosen to distinguish exact bignum arithmetic from truncated arithmetic (still targeting check_bounds/3 only, per the safety instruction).

Mutate read/4 to skip the check_bounds/3 call entirely and go straight to Wasmex.Memory.read_binary/4 -- confirm an existing test catches a malformed pointer no longer being rejected (this should be caught immediately and obviously; if somehow not, that is itself a critical finding to report).

Mutate write/4's implicit length derivation (byte_size(data)) to use a hardcoded small constant instead, and confirm an existing test catches a case where the real data is larger than what gets bounds-checked (a length-confusion bug) -- add a test if none exists.

Confirm the moduledoc-content test (asserting the req165 section 7.2 citation is present) is not trivially satisfiable by a substring that could appear by accident -- check it asserts a sufficiently specific phrase.

Confirm no test in the CURRENT suite, nor any test you add, ever calls a live Wasmex.Memory function with a magnitude >= 2^40 -- state explicitly that you checked every test's literal arguments before finishing, this is non-negotiable given the stakes.
Do not modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex or any other implementation file -- test/fixture files only.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary:
TEST-DESIGNER mutation-driven strengthening pass (WF-02 Step 3) on REQ-168's MemoryGuard -- PASS, 3 real coverage gaps found and closed, all against local mutants only, implementation fully reverted. Baseline: `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs` (with `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"` and `WASMEX_BUILD=true`) showed 15 passed (not the handoff's stated 16 -- a minor prior-report discrepancy, noted not corrected since it isn't in TEST-DESIGNER's scope to reconcile).

AC1 (offset-range >= mutation): mutated check_offset_range/2's guard from `offset > memory_size` to `offset >= memory_size`, ran the suite -- caught immediately by the EXISTING T1 test 'zero-length read exactly at the end-of-memory boundary' (`check_bounds(65536, 0, 65536)` expected `:ok`, mutant returned `{:error, {:offset_out_of_range, 65536, 65536}}`). No new test needed. Reverted and confirmed 15/15 pass again.

AC2 (64-bit-truncated end-of-range mutation): mutated check_end_of_range/3 to compute `range_end = Bitwise.band(offset + length, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)` before comparing. Ran the suite -- ALL existing tests still passed (the existing 2^63-magnitude case doesn't wrap at 2^64, so truncation was invisible to it). This is a real gap: added a new check_bounds/3-only test using `offset=0, length=18_446_744_073_709_551_616` (exactly 2^64, chosen so a 64-bit-truncated sum wraps to 0 and would falsely accept). Verified: against the mutant this returns `:ok` (false accept, confirmed via a temporary IO.inspect probe before turning it into an assertion); against the real (reverted) implementation it correctly returns `{:error, {:length_exceeds_memory, 0, 18446744073709551616, 65536}}`. Re-applied the mutant after adding the assertion and confirmed the new test now fails it (1/17 failed, exact mismatch reported). Reverted; full suite green at 16/16.

AC3 (skip check_bounds/3 in read/4): mutated read/4 to call Wasmex.Memory.read_binary/4 directly with no bounds check. Ran the suite -- caught immediately and obviously by 2 existing T3 tests ('malformed pointer via read/4, offset beyond size' and 'length running past memory end via read/4'), both failing because wasmex's own native bounds check returned a differently-shaped {:memory_access_failed, "out of bounds memory access"} tuple instead of the expected structured {:offset_out_of_range,_}/{:length_exceeds_memory,_} tuples. No new test needed; this is itself a secondary finding worth noting -- wasmex's own native check does still reject these moderate-magnitude out-of-bounds calls cleanly (no crash), consistent with design section 1.3's characterization of 'moderate' magnitudes as already safe at the wasmex layer; MemoryGuard's value is the exact structured-error shape plus safety at magnitudes wasmex's own allocator can't handle, not that these specific moderate-magnitude calls would otherwise crash. Reverted and confirmed 16/16 pass again.

AC4 (write/4 length-confusion mutation): mutated write/4 to hardcode `length = 1` instead of deriving `byte_size(data)`. Ran the suite -- ALL existing tests still passed (16/16): no existing test exercised write/4's length_exceeds_memory path at all, and the existing 'valid round-trip' test writes only 2 bytes, which the mutant's bounds check of length=1 doesn't distinguish from a real bug at this magnitude in a way any existing assertion catches. Real gap: added a new test writing a 10-byte binary at `offset = size - 5` (i.e. real byte_size(data)=10 makes this length_exceeds_memory under a correct bounds check). Verified: against the mutant, the call returns `{:error, {:invalid_pointer, {:memory_access_failed, "out of bounds memory access"}}}` (wasmex's own native check catches the malformed write as a fallback, since the declared length of 1 let it past MemoryGuard's own check) -- confirmed via probe, then via the added assertion (1/17 failed). Against the real (reverted) implementation, returns the clean, pre-native-call `{:error, {:invalid_pointer, {:length_exceeds_memory, size-5, 10, size}}}`, matching the new assertion (17/17 pass). Reverted; final full suite green at 18/18 (after also adding AC5's test below).

AC5 (moduledoc citation specificity): the existing T5 test's three substrings ('does NOT bound a fault' / 'Wasmtime' / 'native code') are specific enough in combination not to be trivially accident-satisfiable, but none of them actually verifies the moduledoc is CITING req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md section 7.2 by name/quote, as design section 6 requires -- prose could independently describe a similar risk without citing that source. Added a second T5 test asserting the literal filename ('req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md'), the literal section marker ('§7.2'), and a regex (tolerant of the moduledoc's own line-wrap whitespace, discovered via one failing run) matching req165's actual verbatim disclosure text ('does not raise, exit, or trap in ... the ordinary BEAM sense'). All 18 tests pass.

AC6 (magnitude safety audit -- explicitly confirmed): read every literal argument to every check_bounds/3, MemoryGuard.read/4, and MemoryGuard.write/4 call across the entire final test file (both pre-existing and newly added). The two magnitude-extreme check_bounds/3 calls (2^63 pre-existing, 2^64 newly added) are pure-function calls only, never live. Every live read/4 and write/4 call in the file uses small/moderate literal arguments (0, 1, 2, 10, 100, 1000, size±1000, size±5, <<99>>, "hi", "x") -- none approaches, let alone reaches, 2^40. No test added by this pass, and no pre-existing test, ever calls a live Wasmex.Memory function at or above that magnitude.

AC7: only test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs and test/specs/REQ-168.md were touched. lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex was mutated repeatedly during this pass but is confirmed byte-for-byte identical to its pre-mutation state (`diff` against a saved original copy showed no differences) before this handoff was finalized.

Final state: `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard_test.exs` -- 18 passed, 0 failed. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, no warnings.

result.safety_confirmation: Every literal argument to every check_bounds/3, read/4, and write/4 call in the final test file was individually checked. Only check_bounds/3 (pure, no Wasmex/NIF dependency) is ever called with a magnitude >= 2^40 (the pre-existing 2^63 case and the newly-added exact-2^64 case). No live Wasmex.Memory-touching call (read/4, write/4, or a direct Wasmex.Memory.* call) anywhere in the file uses a magnitude anywhere near 2^40.
